name.value: D'Arcy Island Campground / BC Marine Trail

description.value: Wilderness island campground in the Haro Strait accessible only by kayak or small boat as part of the BC Marine Trail; notable for its haunting history as BC's leper colony (1891–1924) and Gulf Islands National Park Reserve setting, with no road or bike access, no drinking water on island, and primitive facilities.

address.value: Southern Gulf Islands, BC V0N 2Y0, Canada

raw_osm.description: Gravel tent pads near beach with some shelter in mature forest. Pit toilet. 7 picnic tables. Hammock opportunities. Fee charged May - Sept. No fires, including below high tide mark. No water.
raw_osm.description:approach: Pebble beach. Exposed to SE winds. Strong SE wind may cause hazardous steep surf conditions. Alternative beach, NNE aspect, nearby to N offers longer but easy carry to tent sites.
raw_osm.description:other: Attractive. View. Rough trail across island to historic former leper colony. Gulf Islands National Park Reserve.
raw_osm.name: D'Arcy Island Campground / BC Marine Trail

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The specific OSM URL returns a 404 ('Page not found') because BC Marine Trails has moved its site pages to a member-only interactive map, so OSM tags are the sole evidence source. OSM explicitly states 'Pit toilet' (confirming pit/outhouse toilet present) and 'No water' (confirming no potable water). This is a water-access-only island campground in Gulf Islands National Park Reserve, reachable only by kayak or boat as part of the BC Marine Trail paddling network.
concerns: The specific website URL (https://www.bcmarinetrails.org/map_site/12239) returns a 404 Page Not Found — BC Marine Trails has migrated site detail pages to a members-only interactive map, making online details no longer publicly verifiable via this URL.
This campground is located on an island and is accessible only by water (kayak or boat); it is not reachable by bicycle, which significantly limits its relevance for a cycling tourism directory.
No address, phone, or email present in OSM record.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A real, publicly accessible campground within Gulf Islands National Park Reserve; the OSM record is detailed and the site is actively maintained, despite the specific URL returning 404.
enrichment_extras.notes: OSM tags provide the most complete description available: 7 gravel tent pads, pit toilet, 7 picnic tables, no water, no fires (including below high tide mark), some shelter in mature forest, pebble beach approach exposed to SE winds with alternative NNE beach nearby. Part of Gulf Islands National Park Reserve.
